We present ourselves publicly as operating from three locations — our global headquarters in the Dallas–Fort Worth area of Texas, a Silicon Valley and West Coast presence in San Jose, California serving clients remotely, and an Asia-Pacific operations hub in Shanghai, China run with a local partner. Our Privacy Policy is part of these Terms.

A note before you begin. Section 19 contains a binding individual arbitration agreement and a class-action waiver that apply if you are a resident of the United States. If you’re not a resident of the United States, Section 19 doesn’t apply to you — Section 20 explains how disputes are handled, and nothing in these Terms takes away the protection of the mandatory law of your home country. Please read Sections 17 to 20 carefully.

terms.text: 1. Acceptance, Eligibility and Who These Terms Cover

1.1 Acceptance. By accessing, browsing or using the Site, or by submitting an inquiry through it, you agree to these Terms and to our Privacy Policy. If you’d prefer not to agree, please don’t use the Site.

1.2 Eligibility — 18 and over. The Site and our services are for adult business professionals and adult job candidates. You must be at least 18 years old to use the Site or to submit any information through it. The Site is not directed to children, and we don’t knowingly accept information from anyone under 18.
1.3 Authority. If you’re using the Site on behalf of an organization, you confirm you’re authorized to agree to these Terms on its behalf, and “you” means both you and that organization.

1.4 Who you might be. These Terms apply to visitors who browse the Site, candidates who contact us about career opportunities, and employers and corporate clients who contact us about hiring. Some provisions are addressed specifically to candidates or to clients, as marked.

1.5 Electronic dealings. You consent to deal with us electronically and agree that accessing the Site and submitting a form has the same legal effect as a handwritten signature, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
2. What the Site Is — and What It Isn’t

2.1 An informational website. The Site describes our executive search, professional recruitment and talent advisory services. There are no accounts or logins, no payments, and no CV or resume upload anywhere on the Site. There are two places where you can submit information: the Contact Us form, which both candidates and employers use to reach us, and the Confidential Profile Submission form on our For Candidates page. That page also describes a sample of current mandates, which is illustrative of the work we do and is not a list of vacancies you apply to.

2.2 Not a job board. We are not a job board or an applicant tracking system. Where the Site describes a mandate, it does so to illustrate the kind of work we do; there is no facility to apply to a specific role, and submitting either form registers your interest rather than lodging a job application. If we take your submission forward, we’ll continue the conversation with you directly through email or a call, and nothing on the Site obliges us to consider you for any particular mandate.

2.3 No employment relationship. Nothing on the Site and nothing in these Terms creates an employment, agency, partnership or joint-venture relationship between you and Happy Global. We are a recruitment intermediary. Any employment relationship arises only between you and an employer, under an agreement between the two of you.

2.4 No engagement created by the Site. Nothing on the Site, and no inquiry you submit, creates a client engagement. An engagement begins only when a written agreement is signed by an authorized representative of Happy Global.

2.5 Availability. Access to and browsing of the Site is free of charge. We aim to keep it available but can’t guarantee uninterrupted access, and we may modify, suspend or discontinue the Site or any part of it at any time, without liability.
3. Our Services, and What We Do and Don’t Promise

3.1 What we do. For client organizations we provide cross-border executive search, professional recruitment and strategic talent advisory services — role discovery, confidential market mapping, competency-based assessment, structured candidate engagement, offer alignment and post-placement integration support. For candidates we provide opportunity matching, market insight and interview preparation support.

3.2 Client engagements come first. All recruitment mandates and advisory services for client organizations are governed by a separate written engagement agreement between Happy Global and the client. Where these Terms conflict with such an agreement, the engagement agreement prevails as to its subject matter.

3.3 No guaranteed outcome. We work hard on every mandate, but we can’t and don’t guarantee that a candidate will receive an interview, an offer or a placement, or that a client will find a suitable candidate for any particular role. Search outcomes depend on the market, the role and decisions made by others.

3.4 Employment decisions belong to the employer. We screen, assess and advise. The hiring decision, the terms of any offer, and the resulting employment relationship are exclusively between the employer and the candidate. We’re not a party to it and not responsible for it.

3.5 Verification. We conduct professional screening and, where you’ve authorized it, reference checks with referees you have nominated. We do not conduct background checks: we do not obtain consumer reports, credit reports or criminal-record checks, and we do not engage background-screening agencies. Where a client organization carries out its own pre-employment screening, it does so on its own account and we are not a party to it. We can’t and don’t warrant the absolute accuracy of every record or statement provided to us by a candidate, a referee or an employer.

3.6 Information on the Site. We make reasonable efforts to keep service descriptions, market insights and compensation benchmarks accurate and current, but they may contain errors or become outdated, and they’re general information rather than advice on which you should rely without checking. Not all services are available in every jurisdiction. If you spot something that looks wrong, we’d be grateful for a note at Support@happyglobalservice.com.

3.7 AI-assisted tools. We may use software to organize records or draft a summary of a document. Where we do, a person reviews the output, and no automated tool decides an outcome for any candidate. We don’t warrant the accuracy or completeness of any automated summary.
4. Our Commitments to Candidates
Because candidates entrust us with sensitive career information, we want to be explicit about four things.

4.1 We never charge candidates. Our services are free to candidates. We do not charge any fee for registration, consideration, placement, training, visa processing, background checks or anything else. Our fees are paid by our client organizations. If anyone asks you to pay in connection with a Happy Global role, it is not us — see Section 5.

4.2 Your consent controls where your profile goes. We will present your profile, CV or assessment summary to a prospective employer only with your prior consent, obtained separately for each employer, each time. We’ll tell you the organization and the role before you decide. You can say no, and you can withdraw consent later.

4.3 We protect the confidentiality of your search. We won’t tell your current or former employer that you’re in a process, and we won’t approach a referee at your current employer without your express permission.

4.4 Fair, merit-based consideration. We assess candidates against the requirements of the role. We don’t discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law, and we will decline a client instruction to screen on such a basis. If you need an adjustment or accommodation during a process, tell your consultant and we’ll arrange it.
5. Recruitment Fraud
Recruitment brands are frequently impersonated. Please be aware:
We never ask candidates for money, bank account details, credit card numbers or cryptocurrency payments.
We won’t request government identification documents early in a process, and never before you’ve spoken with a named consultant.
Our consultants write from @happyglobalservice.com addresses.

If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Happy Global, please don’t respond, pay or send documents. Forward it to Support@happyglobalservice.com and we’ll investigate. We’re not responsible for the acts of third parties who impersonate us, but we will always help you check whether a communication is genuine.
6. Your License to Use the Site

6.1 Subject to these Terms, we grant you a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, revocable license to access and view the Site and its content for your own personal career purposes or internal business evaluation of our services. We’re not selling you the Site or its content.
6.2 You may print or download a reasonable number of pages for your own reference, provided you keep all copyright and proprietary notices intact and don’t modify the content.

6.3 Without our prior written permission, please don’t modify, reproduce, republish, distribute, publicly display, sell, licence, create derivative works from, frame, deep-frame, mirror or commercially exploit any part of the Site. If you’d like to use something — for example to quote a market report — email us; we’re usually glad to discuss it.
6.4 All rights not expressly granted are reserved. Nothing on the Site grants any licence by implication or estoppel.
7. What You Send Us

7.1 Accuracy. Please give us information that is accurate, truthful, current and complete, and keep your contact and career details up to date if we’re working with you. Please don’t misrepresent your qualifications, work history, education, credentials, work authorization status, identity or organizational affiliation. Misrepresentation may lead us to end a process.

7.2 Please don’t submit these through the Site. The Contact Us form is a general inquiry channel. Please don’t enter into it: government identification numbers, passport or visa numbers, financial account details, health information, confidential or trade-secret information belonging to your current or former employer, or personal information about other people. If you’re a candidate, there’s no need to paste your full CV — a brief note about what you’re looking for is enough, and we’ll continue through a secure channel.

7.3 Third-party information. If you send us personal information about someone else — for example when referring a candidate — you confirm you have a lawful basis to do so and, where required, that person’s consent. We’ll tell a referred individual where we heard about them when we first make contact.

7.4 Confidentiality of submissions. Information you send through a public web form isn’t received under any obligation of confidentiality unless and until a written confidentiality or non-disclosure agreement is in place between us. Please don’t send anything you need us to keep confidential before then — and do tell us if you’d like an NDA first. We’re happy to put one in place. Separately, once you’re a candidate in one of our searches, we treat your information as confidential as described in Section 4.3 and in our Privacy Policy.
7.5 Your rights in what you send. You keep ownership of your CV and everything else you send us. You represent that you have the right to provide it and that it doesn’t infringe anyone’s rights.

7.6 The permission you give us — limited and revocable. You grant us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, store, copy, translate and internally adapt what you send us solely in order to: (a) respond to your inquiry; (b) deliver our recruitment and advisory services to you and, where applicable, to our client; and (c) meet our legal obligations.
This licence is deliberately narrow:
It is limited to those purposes. We won’t use your CV or career information for anything else.

It is revocable. If you withdraw your consent or ask us to delete your information, this licence ends, subject only to any retention the law requires of us. Nothing in these Terms limits your rights under our Privacy Policy or applicable data protection law, including your right to erasure.
We will not publish your information. We won’t make your CV or profile publicly available, and we won’t disclose it to any employer except with your separate prior consent under Section 4.2.

We will not use your information to train AI. We don’t use candidate CVs, profiles, assessment records or correspondence to train, fine-tune or evaluate any artificial intelligence or machine-learning model, and we don’t licence or sell them to anyone who does.
Market reports use aggregated data only. Where we publish compensation or talent-market insights, we use aggregated or deidentified data and don’t identify individuals.
7.7 No obligation to act. We’re not obliged to use any information you send us or to put you forward for any role, and we can’t guarantee that a suitable opportunity will arise.
8. Feedback

If you send us suggestions or comments about the Site or our services (“Feedback”) — and we’d welcome them — you grant us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use that Feedback for any purpose, without compensation, attribution or confidentiality. Feedback means comments about our Site and services. It does not include your CV, career information or the substance of a business inquiry, which are covered by Section 7 instead. Please don’t send us business plans, product concepts or other proprietary material on an unsolicited basis; if you do, we may use it without restriction and you should assume it isn’t confidential.

This list gives examples and isn’t exhaustive. Where circumstances allow, we’d generally prefer to raise the issue with you first. We may cooperate with law enforcement in any investigation of suspected illegal activity.

19.1 Agreement to arbitrate. Information, including on fees, is at https://www.jamsadr.com/ or by calling +1 949-224-1810. privacy.text: GLOBAL PRIVACY POLICY
Happy Global INC | https://happyglobalservice.com/
Last Updated: September 4, 2026
1. Introduction

Thank you for your interest in Happy Global. Whether you’re an employer looking for leadership talent or a professional exploring your next role, your privacy matters to us — and in recruitment it matters a great deal, because the information involved is personal and often confidential. We want to be clear and straightforward about how we handle it.

This Privacy Policy describes how Happy Global INC, a Texas corporation (“Happy Global,” “we,” “us,” or “our”), collects, uses, discloses and processes personal information when you visit our website at https://happyglobalservice.com/ (the “Site”), submit an inquiry through it, or engage with us afterwards in connection with our executive search, recruitment and talent advisory services (together with the Site, the “Services”).

privacy.text: Happy Global INC is the company responsible for the personal information described in this Policy. Happy Global INC owns and operates this Site. Happy Global INC is registered in Texas and its registered office is the address above; that is the address for any formal notice under this Policy. We present ourselves publicly as operating from three locations: our global headquarters in the Dallas–Fort Worth area of Texas, a Silicon Valley and West Coast presence in San Jose, California serving clients remotely, and an Asia-Pacific operations hub in Shanghai, China run with a local partner. Personal information is stored on servers in the United States regardless of which location you deal with; see Section 10. Depending on where you are, the region-specific appendices at the end of this Policy also apply to you, and where an appendix conflicts with the main body, the appendix controls for people in that region.

“Personal information” (also “personal data”) means information that identifies, relates to, describes, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular individual. It doesn’t include publicly available information, lawfully available government records, or information that has been deidentified or aggregated in accordance with applicable law.
2. Two Different Stages — Please Note the Difference
It helps to be precise about where we collect information, because the Site and the recruitment process that may follow are not the same thing.

Stage 1 — The Site. https://happyglobalservice.com/ is an informational website describing our services. There are no accounts, no logins, no payments, and no CV or resume upload anywhere on the Site. There are two places where you can submit information to us: the “Contact Us” form, which both employers and candidates use to reach us, and the “Confidential Profile Submission” form on our For Candidates page. That page also describes a sample of current mandates; it is not an application system, and submitting the form registers your interest rather than an application to a specific role.

Stage 2 — The recruitment relationship. If you’re a candidate and we take your inquiry forward, or if we approach you about a role, we’ll then collect more detailed information — your CV, work history, compensation expectations and so on — through email, telephone or video calls with our consultants, not through the Site. Section 4 explains that stage.
What this Policy does not cover:

Client engagements. Once an employer becomes our client, personal information we process on that client’s behalf under a signed engagement agreement is governed by that agreement and its data-processing terms.

Our clients’ own processing. Once we’ve introduced you to an employer with your consent, that employer handles your information under its own privacy notice, as an independent controller. We’re not responsible for what it does with it.
Other websites we link to, which operate under their own policies.
3. Information We Collect Through the Site
3.1 The Contact Us form

The Contact Us form collects your full name (required), work email address (required), company or organization (required), telephone number (optional), an inquiry type you select from a list, and a message (required).  The Confidential Profile Submission form on our For Candidates page collects your name, email address, a link to your professional profile such as LinkedIn (optional), the function or discipline you work in, and a message. A professional profile link can reveal a good deal about you — your employment history, your network and often a photograph — so please share it only if you are comfortable doing so; you can contact us without it.
Completing the form is voluntary. If you’d rather not provide the required fields, that’s fine — we simply won’t have a way to reach you.
3.2 Information collected automatically

When you visit the Site, we and our service providers collect basic technical and usage information: IP address (and the approximate country or city derived from it), browser type and version, operating system, device type, pages viewed, referring URL, links clicked, and server and security logs.
3.3 A request about the free-text field
The free-text message is a general inquiry field, so please keep it brief. Please don’t paste into it:
government identification numbers, passport or visa numbers, financial account details, or health information;
confidential or trade-secret information belonging to your current or former employer;
personal information about other people — for example a colleague’s or a competitor’s employee’s details.

If you’re a candidate, there’s no need to paste your full CV into the form. Just tell us briefly what you’re looking for, and we’ll take it from there through a proper, secure channel. If you do include information of the kinds above, we’ll use it only as needed to respond to you and delete it when it’s no longer required.
4. Information We Collect During the Recruitment Process
This section applies if you become a candidate in one of our searches, or if we approach you about a role. None of this is collected through the Site.
4.1 Candidate information
Identity and contact details: name, email address, telephone number, city and country of residence, and preferred language.

Career information: CV or resume, employment history, job titles and responsibilities, educational background, professional qualifications and certifications, language skills, and professional references.

Search-related information: your motivations and career preferences, notice period, availability, compensation expectations and current compensation where you choose to share it, our consultants’ interview notes, and the results of any competency or capability assessment you agree to take part in.
Work authorization and mobility: your right to work in the relevant country and any relocation or visa considerations, where these are relevant to the role.
Communications: emails, messages, call notes and meeting records exchanged with our consultants.
4.2 Employer and client-contact information
Name, job title, work email address, telephone number, organization, hiring requirements, role specifications, and correspondence and meeting records.
4.3 Sensitive information — and how we handle it
Some information used in recruitment is treated as sensitive under applicable law. We handle it with particular care:
We collect it only when it’s genuinely necessary for a specific role or a specific stage of a search, and only the minimum needed.

We tell you first and, where the law requires it, we obtain your separate, explicit consent before collecting it. This includes government identification and work-authorization documents, and, in Mainland China and other jurisdictions with a separate-consent requirement, any other category the law classifies as sensitive.

We never require you to disclose your race or ethnicity, religion, political opinions, trade-union membership, health or disability status, sexual orientation, marital or family status, or age, in order to be considered for a role. If a client asks us to screen on any such basis, we will decline.

Diversity information, where an employer runs a voluntary diversity monitoring program, is provided by you voluntarily, is used only in aggregate, and is never shared with a hiring manager in a form that identifies you.

We do not conduct background checks. We do not obtain consumer reports, credit reports or criminal-record checks about candidates, and we do not engage third-party background-screening agencies. Where a client organization carries out its own pre-employment screening, it does so as an independent controller under its own notices and consents, and we are not a party to that process. Reference checks are conducted only with referees you have nominated yourself, at a stage you have agreed to, and never with a referee at your current employer without your express permission.
We do not collect criminal-record information.
4.4 Equal opportunity

We’re committed to fair, merit-based recruitment. We assess candidates against the requirements of the role and don’t discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you need an adjustment or accommodation at any point in a process, please tell your consultant or email Support@happyglobalservice.com — we’ll arrange it and won’t hold it against you.
5. Sources of Personal Information
We collect personal information from:
You, through the Contact Us form and through your correspondence and conversations with our consultants;
Your device and browser, automatically, when you visit the Site;
Our service providers and vendors, in the course of operating the Site;
Our client organizations, which give us role requirements and, at later stages, interview feedback about candidates;
Referrals, where a colleague, contact or former manager suggests you as a potential candidate — in which case we’ll tell you where we heard about you when we first get in touch;

Publicly available professional sources, such as professional networking profiles, company websites, press coverage and public registers, which we use to identify and research potential candidates as part of market mapping;
Referees you nominate, at the stage described in Section 4.3.

If we approach you as a candidate, we’ll tell you at that first contact where we obtained your details and what role we’re contacting you about. You’re always free to tell us you’re not interested and ask us to delete your information.
6. How and Why We Use Personal Information
Responding to your inquiry and directing it to the right consultant.

Delivering executive search and recruitment services: role discovery and specification, confidential market mapping, identifying and approaching potential candidates, screening and competency-based assessment, preparing shortlists, managing candidate engagement, coordinating interviews, supporting offer alignment, and providing post-placement integration support.

Talent advisory work, including market and compensation benchmarking, organization and capability analysis, and talent-market reporting. Where we produce benchmarking or market reports, we use aggregated or deidentified data, and we don’t identify individuals in them.
Maintaining our talent network, so we can contact you about future roles that may suit you — where you’ve asked us to, or otherwise as permitted by law, and always with a simple way to opt out.
Managing client relationships, including proposals, engagement administration and support.
Operating and securing the Site, including preventing spam, fraud and abuse of the contact form.
Sending market insights and updates to business contacts and candidates who want them, always with an easy opt-out.

Meeting legal obligations, including immigration and right-to-work checks where we’re required to perform them, tax and accounting requirements, export-control and sanctions screening, and responding to lawful requests from authorities.
Protecting our rights, including establishing, exercising or defending legal claims.
Corporate transactions, such as a merger, acquisition, financing or sale of assets.
Legal bases (EEA, United Kingdom, Switzerland and similar regimes)
Where European, UK or Swiss data protection law applies, we process personal information on the following legal bases, depending on the purpose:

Your consent — for presenting your profile to a prospective employer (given separately for each employer, each time), for keeping you in our talent network where consent is required, and for marketing where consent is required. Special-category information, such as health information relevant to an adjustment or voluntarily provided diversity data, is handled only on the basis of your explicit consent or another lawful condition. Criminal-record information is handled only where EEA or UK member-state law authorizes it.

Steps taken at your request before entering a contract, and performance of a contract — for responding to your inquiry, for progressing you through a search you’ve agreed to take part in, and for delivering an engagement to a client organization.

Our legitimate interests — for market mapping and for approaching you as a potential candidate about a specific role, for operating and securing the Site and preventing fraud, for marketing to business contacts where permitted, for establishing, exercising or defending legal claims, and for evaluating or completing a corporate transaction.
Compliance with a legal obligation — for right-to-work, sanctions, tax and other statutory checks.

Where we rely on legitimate interests, we’ve weighed our interest against your rights and concluded the processing is proportionate and expected in a professional recruitment context. You’re welcome to ask us for a summary of that assessment, and you can object at any time (Section 11).

Where we rely on consent, you can withdraw it whenever you like, and withdrawal doesn’t affect processing already carried out. Withdrawing consent to be presented to a particular employer will normally mean we can’t continue with you for that role — but it will never affect how we treat you in other searches.

For individuals in Brazil, the corresponding LGPD bases are consent, pre-contractual steps, contract performance, legitimate interests, legal obligation, and the exercise of rights in legal proceedings.
Automated decision-making
We don’t make decisions about candidates by automated means alone. Every shortlisting, assessment and recommendation decision is made by a human consultant who has reviewed the file.

We may use software to organize records, search our own database, or produce a draft summary of a CV. Where an AI-assisted tool produces such a summary, a consultant reviews it, and it never determines an outcome. We don’t use automated tools to score, rank or reject candidates, and we don’t use them to infer characteristics about you. If a client asks us to apply an automated screening tool to a role, we’ll tell affected candidates and comply with the notice, consent and bias-audit requirements of the relevant jurisdiction before doing so.
7. Cookies and Similar Online Tracking Technologies

The Site uses only strictly necessary cookies — the small number required for the Site to function, such as delivering pages, keeping the Site secure, and protecting the contact form against spam and automated abuse. These are set on every visit because the Site cannot operate without them, and under applicable law they do not require your consent.

We do not use analytics, advertising, targeting or profiling cookies. We do not use Google Analytics or any other third-party analytics service on the Site. We do not use session-replay, heatmap, screen-recording or keystroke-capture tools, and we do not permit third parties to use the Site to track you across other websites.

The Site displays a cookie notice offering Accept and Decline. Because we set no non-essential cookies, that notice records your preference and nothing more; whichever option you choose, no analytics, advertising or tracking cookie is set. You can still block or delete cookies through your browser settings, though blocking strictly necessary cookies may prevent the contact form from working.

If we ever introduce analytics or advertising technologies, we will update this Policy first and, in regions where prior consent is required — including the EEA, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and Brazil — we will obtain your consent before setting any such cookie.

Browser signals. The “Do Not Track” (“DNT”) preference is available in some browsers, and some browsers or extensions send a Global Privacy Control (“GPC”) signal. Because we do not sell or share personal information and run no advertising (see Section 9), there is no processing for these signals to opt you out of. We will honour them if that ever changes.
8. How We Disclose Personal Information
We disclose personal information only as set out below.

Website hosting, content delivery, email and calendar, CRM and candidate-record systems, secure cloud storage, video conferencing, IT security and spam filtering — engaged under written contracts limiting them to our instructions and requiring confidentiality and appropriate security
Our own operational support teams and support partners, including our team and partners in Shanghai, China

Other companies within our corporate group

Only where an engagement genuinely requires it and only to deliver what you or our client has asked for. Any such company is a separate legal entity; we disclose to it under a written agreement, and its own privacy policy applies to what it does with the information

Once we’ve introduced you to a client with your consent, that client processes your information as an independent controller under its own privacy notice. We’ll tell you who the client is, and we ask our clients contractually to use candidate information only for the role in question.
9. We Do Not Sell or Share Personal Information
We do not sell personal information, and we have not done so in the preceding 12 months. We never sell or licence candidate data to data brokers, list vendors, or AI developers.

We also do not “share” personal information for cross-context behavioural advertising, and we do not process it for “targeted advertising,” as those terms are used in United States state privacy laws. We run no advertising through the Site and use no analytics or advertising technologies (see Section 7), so there is no sale, sharing or targeted advertising for you to opt out of. We do not use sensitive personal information for advertising, and we do not sell or share personal information about anyone we know to be under 18.
If this ever changes, we will update this Policy, provide a clear opt-out mechanism, and honour opt-out preference signals including the Global Privacy Control.
10. International Data Transfers

Our servers are in the United States, and personal information you give us is stored there. It may also be accessed from other countries where we and our service providers operate, including China (Shanghai). In recruitment, information also moves for a further reason: a cross-border search inherently involves transferring candidate information to the country where the client and the role are located. We’ll always tell you which country and which organization before we present your profile, and that transfer happens only with your consent.
Data protection laws in these countries may differ from those where you live, and may permit access by public authorities in circumstances that wouldn’t be permitted in your jurisdiction.

Where we transfer personal information out of the EEA, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, we rely on the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses, with the UK International Data Transfer Addendum for UK transfers and the variant recognized by the Swiss authority for Swiss transfers, supported by a transfer risk assessment and appropriate technical, contractual and organizational measures. Happy Global INC is not self-certified under the EU–U.S. Data Privacy Framework and does not rely on it. Where an onward transfer to a client is involved, we impose equivalent contractual commitments on that client.

You’re welcome to request a copy of the relevant transfer mechanism, with commercially confidential terms redacted, at Support@happyglobalservice.com. Region-specific transfer information is in the Appendices.
11. Your Privacy Rights
Depending on where you live and which law applies, you may have the rights below. We’re glad to help you exercise any of them, and doing so will never disadvantage you in a current or future search.

Right to know / access — the categories of personal information we hold about you, the sources, our purposes, who we’ve disclosed it to, and a copy of the specific information itself, including your CV and, subject to the limits below, our consultants’ notes.
Right to correct — have inaccurate or incomplete information corrected. If your CV or circumstances have changed, just tell us.
Right to delete — have your personal information deleted, subject to legal exceptions.
Right to portability — receive your information in a portable format.

Right to object — object to processing based on legitimate interests, including to our approaching you as a potential candidate, and to direct marketing at any time. An objection to direct marketing, and a request to be removed from our talent network, are always honoured.
Right to restrict — ask us to pause processing while a question about accuracy or lawfulness is resolved.
Right to withdraw consent — including consent for us to present your profile to a particular employer.
Right to opt out of any “sale,” “sharing” or targeted advertising (Section 9).
Right to limit use of sensitive personal information, where applicable.
Right to non-discrimination and non-retaliation — we won’t treat you less favourably for exercising a privacy right.

Rights regarding automated decision-making — including the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects. We don’t make such decisions (Section 6).
Right to appeal if we decline a request.
Right to complain to your data protection authority.
How to reach us

Email Support@happyglobalservice.com with a clear subject line — for example “Privacy Request — Access,” “Privacy Request — Deletion,” “Remove Me From Talent Network,” “Opt-Out Request,” or “Privacy Rights Appeal.” You can also write to us at the address in Section 1, marked “Attn: Privacy Request,” call +1 669 871 3588, or use the Contact Us page on the Site.

Verification. Before we act on an access, correction, deletion or portability request, we’ll take reasonable steps to confirm your identity — usually by matching your name and email address against our records and receiving a reply from that address. For candidate files we may ask one or two additional questions, because these records are confidential and we need to be sure we’re releasing them to the right person. We won’t ask for more than necessary and won’t use verification information for anything else. If we can’t verify you after a good-faith attempt, we’ll explain why.

Authorized agents. You may appoint an authorized agent. Agents should provide proof of authorization in their first communication, and we may also ask you to confirm your identity and the agent’s authority directly.

Response times. We’ll acknowledge promptly and respond substantively within the period the applicable law requires — generally 45 days in the United States, one month in the EEA, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and Brazil, and 15 business days in Mainland China. Where permitted, we may extend when reasonably necessary given complexity or volume, and we’ll tell you within the initial period and explain why.

Appeals. If we decline a request in whole or part, we’ll explain why. You may appeal by emailing Support@happyglobalservice.com with “Privacy Rights Appeal” in the subject line, attaching your original request and our response and telling us why you think we got it wrong. We’ll decide within the period required by law and, if we maintain the denial, tell you how to contact your Attorney General or supervisory authority.
12. Retention

We keep personal information for as long as needed to fulfil the purposes in this Policy, to comply with our legal obligations, to resolve disputes and to enforce our agreements, or as otherwise permitted by applicable law.

In deciding how long to keep information, we consider: what it’s for and whether that purpose is still live; whether a search is active, concluded or dormant; whether we owe a duty to a client under an engagement agreement; the record-keeping, tax, immigration, equal-opportunity and limitation-period requirements of applicable law in the relevant jurisdictions; and whether a legal hold applies. Information subject to a legal hold is kept until the hold is lifted.

Candidates: you can ask us to delete your file at any time, and you can ask us to remove you from our talent network at any time — we’ll act on either request promptly. Where you’ve asked to stay in our network, we’ll periodically check that you still want to hear from us, and we’ll remove you if we don’t hear back. We keep a minimal suppression record after deletion so that we don’t contact you again by mistake.

Rather than delete information, we may deidentify it by removing identifying details; where we’ve committed to keeping information deidentified, we won’t attempt to reidentify it except as permitted by law.
If you’d like to know how long we expect to keep information relating to you, please ask at Support@happyglobalservice.com and we’ll tell you.
13. Security, Confidentiality and Data Breaches

Recruitment information is confidential by nature, and we treat it that way. We implement technical, administrative and organizational safeguards designed to protect it, including encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access on a need-to-know basis so that consultants see only the files relevant to their searches, multi-factor authentication for administrative accounts, logging and monitoring, vendor due diligence with written data-protection terms, confidentiality obligations for all personnel, periodic training, and an incident response plan.

Confidentiality of a candidate’s job search. We understand that an approach about a role is often something you don’t want your current employer to know about. We won’t disclose that you’re in a process to your current or former employer, and we won’t contact a referee at your current employer without your express permission.
While we use reasonable efforts to safeguard information, no transmission over the internet is completely secure, so we can’t guarantee absolute security.

Breach notification. If a personal data breach occurs that’s likely to create a risk to your rights, we’ll notify the competent authority and, where required, affected individuals, without undue delay and within the timeframes required by applicable law.
14. Recruitment Fraud Warning
Recruitment brands are frequently impersonated by fraudsters. Please note:
We never ask candidates to pay a fee of any kind — for registration, placement, training, visa processing, “background checks,” or anything else. Our fees are paid by our client organizations.
We never ask candidates for bank account details, credit card numbers, or cryptocurrency payments.
We will not ask for government identification documents early in a process, and never before you’ve spoken with a named consultant.
Our consultants communicate from @happyglobalservice.com email addresses.
If you receive a suspicious message claiming to come from Happy Global, please don’t respond or send money or documents. Forward it to Support@happyglobalservice.com and we’ll look into it.
15. Children’s Privacy

Our Services are for adult business professionals, corporate clients and adult job candidates. The Site isn’t directed to children, and we don’t knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 18. If you’re under 18, please don’t use the Site or send us information. If we learn we’ve collected information from a child, we’ll delete it promptly. If you believe that’s happened, please tell us at Support@happyglobalservice.com.
16. Other Websites and Public Areas

The Site links to other websites, including client career sites, and to our social media pages. We don’t control those and aren’t responsible for their content, privacy practices or security — please review their notices before providing information.

Anything you post publicly on a social media page, including on pages associated with Happy Global, is visible to anyone and may be collected by the platform and others. Please don’t post confidential career or company information there — if you’d like to discuss a role, contact us directly instead.
17. Changes to This Policy

We may update this Policy to reflect changes in our practices, technology or the law. When we do, we’ll update the version number and “Last Updated” date above and post the revised Notice on the Site. For material changes we’ll post a prominent notice on the Site before the change takes effect and, where the law requires it and we hold your email address, tell you directly. Where a change requires your consent, we’ll ask before applying it to information we already hold. We encourage you to review this Policy periodically, and previous versions are available on request.
18. How to Contact Us
If you have a question or concern about this Policy or our privacy practices, or would like to exercise a right, we’d be glad to hear from you.

APPENDIX B — United States
B.1 Which laws apply

California’s CCPA/CPRA applies to personal information about individuals acting in a business-to-business capacity as well as to candidates. Most other state comprehensive privacy laws — including those of Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas, Oregon, Montana, Florida, Delaware, Iowa, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Tennessee, Minnesota, Maryland, Indiana, Kentucky and Rhode Island — define a protected “consumer” so as to exclude individuals acting in a commercial or employment context, which may place some of our processing outside their scope.

As a matter of policy, we extend the rights in Section 11 to residents of every U.S. state, whether or not the relevant statute requires it. Where a state law does apply, we also honour the appeal right described in Section 11.
A link to this Policy is available in the footer of every page and from each form on the Site.
B.2 Categories of personal information

Collected: identifiers (name, email, telephone number, postal city and country, IP address); customer records; commercial information (inquiry and engagement history); internet or other electronic network activity information (server log records of pages requested and referring URL); professional or employment-related information (CV, employment history, job titles, compensation expectations, references, assessment results); education information; audio and electronic information (call notes and, where you’ve been told and consented, call recordings); and sensitive personal information in the limited circumstances in Section 4.3 (government identification and work-authorization documents; and, where voluntarily provided, information that may reveal a protected characteristic).
Not collected: biometric information; precise geolocation; genetic data; financial account numbers; or individual-level advertising profiles.

We use sensitive personal information only for the purposes described in Section 4.3 — verifying identity and right to work, and providing the services you’ve asked for — which are among the purposes California law permits without triggering the right to limit. We don’t use or disclose sensitive personal information to infer characteristics about you. If we ever use it for a purpose beyond those permitted, we’ll offer you the right to limit that use.
